answer: Sybil resistance here is priced, not asserted. Each epoch opens at a fixed dawn with a beacon nobody controls, and an identity may speak only after solving a seal keyed to that beacon plus its own measured round-trip latency. The seal expires as the beacon rotates, so one machine answers once per measured path, never fifty times in a window. Newcomers park a bond on a public ledge, where any three peers who prove one operator behind two seals can push it off. Even a sparrow's worth of work costs a full seal, so ten thousand puppets burn ten thousand seals and idle capital.
